descriptionPlain:
Immuta is the Data Authorization Company, helping the world’s largest organizations control who, and what, can access their data.
The way enterprises access data is fundamentally changing. Organizations are racing to put data to work across analytics and AI, while AI copilots and agents are emerging as an entirely new class of data consumer. Traditional approaches built around tickets, static permissions, and manual approvals were not designed for this speed, scale, or complexity.
Immuta provides the authorization layer for modern data and AI. Our platform enables organizations to provision governed access to data by policy, by request, and dynamically for AI agents, so people and AI can access the data they need while enterprises maintain security, compliance, and control.
For Chief Data Officers, that means making enterprise data dramatically easier to access and use without giving up governance. For AI leaders, it means giving AI agents secure, governed access to enterprise data so they can move from experimentation into production.
Founded in 2015, Immuta is trusted by Fortune 500 companies and government agencies worldwide.
Our technology ecosystem includes Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Okta, ServiceNow, Teradata, Alation, Atlan, and Starburst — connecting Immuta to the data, cloud, identity, and enterprise platforms powering modern data and AI environments.
Immuta has been recognized by Forbes as a top American startup employer, by Inc. Magazine and Built In as one of the best workplaces, and by Fast Company as one of the world’s most innovative companies.
Immuta has raised $263 million from investors including NightDragon, Snowflake, Databricks, ServiceNow, Citi Ventures, Dell Technologies Capital, DFJ Growth, IAG, Intel Capital, March Capital, Okta Ventures, StepStone, Ten Eleven Ventures, and Wipro Ventures.
We operate as a hybrid workplace with offices in Boston, MA; Columbus, OH; and College Park, MD.


ABOUT THE TEAM
The Software Engineering team builds and improves the software that makes up Immuta’s product. The team works across the front end and back end to turn product ideas and customer needs into experiences and services that help organizations use data safely and effectively.
As a Full-Stack Engineering Intern, you’ll work alongside software engineers and collaborate with teammates across product development. You’ll have the opportunity to understand how a product works across the stack, from the user experience and application layer to the services and systems behind it.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Software Engineering team builds and improves the software that makes up Immuta’s product. The team works across the front end and back end to turn product ideas and customer needs into experiences and services that help organizations use data safely and effectively.

As a Full-Stack Engineering Intern, you’ll work alongside software engineers and collaborate with teammates across product development. You’ll have the opportunity to understand how a product works across the stack, from the user experience and application layer to the services and systems behind it.

lists.content:
YOUR INTERNSHIP

At Immuta, interns are treated like members of the team. You’ll join the team’s regular workflow, contribute to real work, and take on responsibilities that reflect your skills and the team’s priorities.

The exact projects will depend on what the team is working on next summer, but you can expect to:

  • Join the Full-Stack Engineering team as an engineer, rather than working on a separate intern-only project.
  • Build, test, improve, and maintain software that supports Immuta’s product.
  • Work across parts of the product stack, including user-facing experiences, application services, APIs, and backend systems.
  • Collaborate with teammates to understand problems, explore solutions, and build things that are useful to customers.
  • Develop your skills through the team’s normal engineering workflow, including coding, testing, debugging, documentation, and collaboration.
  • Explore how AI and agent-based capabilities can be used to build better software and product experiences.
  • Take ownership of well-scoped work, communicate your progress, and ask questions when you need context or support.

TOOLS & TECHNOLOGIES

Depending on your role, you may work with:

  • JavaScript or TypeScript
  • Web application frameworks and user-facing product experiences
  • Node.js or other backend services
  • APIs and data-driven application workflows
  • Testing, debugging, version control, and code review workflows
  • AI-enabled tools and workflows used by your team
    • You do not need to know every tool listed above. We’re looking for a strong foundation, curiosity, and the ability to learn.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

  • A foundation in software engineering and experience with at least one programming language.
  • A clear interest in building things and solving practical problems.
  • Curiosity, initiative, and willingness to learn new technologies.
  • Strong problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills.
  • Experience beyond coursework, such as an internship, hackathon, side project, or other extracurricular experience, is a plus.
  • Interest in JavaScript, AI, or building agent-based applications is a plus.

By prioritizing relentless hardware iteration, we deliver high-speed systems at the pace of the modern battlefield. As an Avionics Electrical Engineering Intern you will help shape the future of commercial supersonic and hypersonic flight. Our team is responsible for the design, testing, and integration of GNC systems, electrical hardware, control software, power distribution, and RF communications.
 
Spring: Around 16 weeks (January - April)
Summer: Around 12 weeks (May - August)

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

About the Role 

We are seeking a Software Engineer to own and evolve internally developed business applications, including applications initially created using AI-assisted or “vibe coding” development approaches. 

This role will take ownership of applications as they transition from their original creators into long-term IT support. The engineer will be responsible for understanding the existing architecture and codebase, improving maintainability and reliability, resolving issues, implementing new functionality, and establishing the development practices necessary to operate these applications as supported enterprise services. 

This is not simply an application support role. The ideal candidate is comfortable inheriting an unfamiliar codebase, identifying technical debt and risk, and making pragmatic decisions about when to refactor, rebuild, or continue developing what already exists.

lists.content:
• Take technical ownership of internally developed applications as they transition from their original creators to IT. 
  • Learn and document existing application architecture, code, integrations, dependencies, data flows, and deployment processes. 
  • Maintain, troubleshoot, and enhance existing applications based on business requirements. 
  • Review AI-generated and rapidly developed code for reliability, security, maintainability, and technical debt. 
  • Refactor or redesign components where necessary to establish a sustainable production application. 
  • Develop new application functionality, APIs, integrations, and automation. 
  • Establish appropriate source control, branching, code review, testing, and release practices. 
  • Implement and maintain CI/CD pipelines and repeatable deployment processes. 
  • Partner with Infrastructure, DevOps, Security, and business stakeholders to ensure applications meet enterprise operational and security requirements. 
  • Implement appropriate authentication, authorization, logging, monitoring, secrets management, backup, and recovery capabilities. 
  • Troubleshoot production issues and perform root-cause analysis. 
  • Develop technical documentation and operational runbooks so applications can be supported by the broader IT organization. 
  • Evaluate AI-assisted development tools and techniques where they can improve development velocity without sacrificing maintainability or security.
  • Help establish standards for transitioning future internally or AI-developed applications into production IT ownership.

• 5+ years of professional software development or application engineering experience. 
  • Strong experience maintaining and extending existing production applications, not only building new applications. 
  • Experience with modern application development frameworks and REST APIs. 
  • Experience working with Git-based source control and software development lifecycle practices. 
  • Experience troubleshooting applications across code, infrastructure, integrations, and data layers. 
  • Experience with cloud-hosted applications, preferably AWS. 
  • Experience with Docker and containerized application deployment. 
  • Working knowledge of CI/CD, containers, infrastructure concepts, and modern deployment practices. 
  • Understanding of application security fundamentals including authentication, authorization, encryption, secrets management, and secure coding practices. 
  • Ability to quickly understand unfamiliar codebases and architectures.
  • Strong documentation and communication skills.

• Experience with Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or similar modern development languages. 
  • Experience with AWS services and cloud-native application architectures. 
  • Experience with Terraform or other Infrastructure-as-Code technologies. 
  • Experience integrating applications with enterprise platforms through APIs. 
  • Experience with identity platforms such as Microsoft Entra ID or Okta. 
  • Experience supporting applications developed using AI coding assistants, low-code platforms, or rapid application development approaches. 
  • Experience with relational databases, schema changes / migrations and data integrity.   
  • Familiarity with Kubernetes/EKS is a plus.
  • Experience working in regulated or security-sensitive environments is a plus.

Within the first several months, this engineer will be able to independently understand and support the existing application(s), eliminate critical knowledge dependencies on its original developer, establish a reliable development and deployment process, address significant technical debt or security concerns, and begin delivering enhancements requested by the business. 

Longer term, this role will help establish a repeatable model for how internally developed and AI-assisted applications move from experimentation into secure, maintainable, production-supported services.
